title: The shorter label
bodyMd:
A fictional museum shortened the labels beside its exhibits after visitors complained of fatigue. Staff expected more people to finish reading them. Observations showed that visitors spent less time at individual displays but discussed objects with companions more often. The museum could not tell from time spent alone whether engagement had increased or decreased.

It tested a second design: a short introductory label with an optional longer text nearby. Some visitors read only the introduction, while others used it to decide whether to continue. Curators resisted describing one group as serious and the other as superficial. A visitor might bring extensive prior knowledge, have limited time, or prefer conversation to silent reading. The new design offered different routes into the material without assuming that all attention should look the same.
